section1:
EDIT/OUTPAINT THE ATTACHED SQUARE IN PLACE, preserving its exact camera, geometry, framing and texture scale. This is a game terrain texture, not an illustration redesign. Output a single square at the highest available resolution, ideally 2048 x 2048.
The attached image is a template. Its left 46% is existing artwork, and the white area on the right needs new terrain. Do not move or zoom the existing artwork. The first 21% of image width MUST remain unchanged: the actual path enters the left edge centered at 51% of image height and slopes diagonally down/right. Preserve this left-hand path position and stone positions faithfully. Do not move the entrance upward.
In the rest of the image, remove the old black boundary fade and replace ALL white/black areas with natural seamless continuations of this EXACT ground art. Continue the stone path on its diagonal in the first 25%, then gently turn it right so it leaves the RIGHT edge centered at 75% of image height. Same pathway width and sharp cream/tan/grey irregular cobbles as the input. There is one simple curved path, no crossroads, no circle, no disconnected paths.
Match the exact camp ground: warm ochre soil, flat dry orange/brown leaf litter, tiny gravel and specks of muted olive moss. Keep the surface richly but crisply painted, with the same size leaves and stones as the original. The upper-right ground can include one irregular open patch of slightly more bare soil to place future resource assets, but no objects in it. Maintain the ground colour from left to right, neutral overhead light and a flat overhead camera.
No text, framing, map borders, black vignette on the new terrain, blur, blurry paths, perspective changes, grids or divisions. No trees, shrubs, tall plants, rocks, wood, stumps, puddles, water, buildings, walls, people, fire, shadows from absent props or any placed assets. Only the ground layer. Preserve source textures on the left; outpaint the new right area.
section2:
Use case: precise-object-edit, terrain outpainting. EDIT THE ATTACHED TEMPLATE IN PLACE. Single opaque rectangular game terrain image, same 1792:1536 aspect ratio, highest detail.
This is the next adjoining piece of an existing top-down game terrain. The LEFT 256 pixels (14.286% of width) contain the exact right edge of the previous section. The rest is blank WHITE to extend. Keep that entire left strip at its existing location, scale and colour. Do NOT zoom, crop, recenter, duplicate or move it. Preserve its small leaves and stones. Extend its artwork naturally through all the white space.
The existing cobblestone path is centered at about 75% of image height on the left. Continue it seamlessly at exactly that height and width (roughly 200 pixels at input scale) for the first third, then let it wind gently upward toward the RIGHT edge centered around 65% of height. Same clearly separated sharp cream, warm grey and buff rounded paving stones and dark joints.
In the right two-thirds, a narrower worn DIRT footpath branches naturally from the cobbled path and curves north, leaving the top at about 72% of image width. This is a small woodland route toward a future industrial scrapyard, with a north fork toward a later district. Leave some naturally shaped patches of relatively bare flat earth beside the paths for future separately placed resources.
EXACTLY match input's ground-art style and material scale: warm ochre soil, richly painted fine grit, tiny embedded pebbles, scattered flat dry orange/brown fallen leaves, hints of flat subdued olive-green moss in irregular patches. No sudden colour change, no greener colour stripe. Soft even overhead lighting. Top-down flat ground plane, crisp painted contours, no blur or depth-of-field. Full detailed terrain right to ALL edges.
No black fade, white gaps, rectangular clearing, borders, panels, grid, text, symbols, map labels, watermark, trees, shrubs, raised grass, upright plants, tree shadows, resource rocks, wood, stumps, logs, puddles or water, buildings, walls, characters or props. Only ground, embedded stone walkway and dirt path. Preserve the original left strip faithfully so the join is invisible.
